h: Who stayed with Lula, and who shifted
t:
On 4 October 2026 Flávio Bolsonaro took 47.0% of the valid vote and Lula 45.2%. Four years earlier Lula had led Jair Bolsonaro 48.4% to 43.2%.

Every dot here is 250 people at the polling place where they vote: blue for the Bolsonaro camp, red for Lula, amber for those on the roll who didn't vote, grey for everyone else. Scroll to follow where the vote moved.

h: A blue drift, not a new map
t:
2022 is left of the divider, 2026 right. Drag it to compare. The broad geography held: a red Northeast, a blue South and Centre-West, a mixed Southeast. Lula's share fell 3.3 points and the Bolsonaro camp's rose 3.8, a fairly even drift on top of the same map.

The ballot is secret, so this story is about places, not people. When a place shifted, we can't tell who in it changed their vote.

Did Lula's voters stay home? Abstention barely moved: 21.0% of the roll in 2022, 21.1% in 2026. The 3.4 million votes Lula lost sit beside 5.0 million that the Bolsonaro camp gained.

And abstention fell where Lula is strongest: down 2.5 points in the poorest quarter of municipalities, up 0.9 in the richest.

Lula's share in the Northeast slipped from 66.8% to 63.8%, about the national fall but from a far higher base. Because turnout rose there (abstention fell 1.1 points), he lost only about 260,000 votes in the whole region.

Here only the smallest quarter of municipalities is lit, under about 5,200 people each. The totals above add up just these places. In municipalities under 10,000 people Lula's share fell 6.5 points; in the 15 cities over a million, 0.6.

Across the 27 state capitals Lula's share fell only 0.6 points, against 4.1 everywhere else. In eleven of them it rose, Rio de Janeiro among them (43.5% to 43.9%), and Recife, Fortaleza, Belém and Brasília too.

The biggest fall of any state was in Goiás, −8.5 points, and Aparecida de Goiânia fell 8.3. But here the loss didn't go mainly to Flávio. Ronaldo Caiado, the state's former governor, took 12.3% in Goiás: watch the grey dots grow on the 2026 side.
The South fell furthest as a region, −5.5 points, and Rio Grande do Sul −6.6. In Caxias do Sul and the Serra Gaúcha Lula's share fell about 5 points, and abstention rose rather than fell.

h: Inside the city: the richest neighbourhoods
t: A city is not one place. Here only the polling places in the richest quarter of neighbourhoods are lit, by household-head income in the Census tracts within 1 km. Most sit in São Paulo's centre and south-west. The totals above are for these polling places across the whole country.
Now the poorest quarter: the periphery lights up and the centre goes dark. Compare the totals above with the last step: the same city, a different electorate.

The most Evangelical quarter of municipalities, where 29.5% or more of residents are Evangelical, didn't stand out: Lula's share there fell 3.3 points, the national figure. It fell most in the most Catholic, mostly rural quarter (−5.3) and least where many report no religion (−2.5), which are mostly big cities.

Religion describes places, not voters: this doesn't show how Evangelicals voted.

One in five people on the roll didn't vote, but not all of them had to. Split by age: 18–69, who are required to vote, are 14.7% of the roll; 16–17 and 70–79, for whom voting is optional, 3.5%; and 80+, 2.8%. The 2026 split is estimated.

The 2026 roll lists 297,977 voters aged 100 or more, and 99% of that age group didn't vote in 2022. Some of the 80+ abstainers are people no longer living. Leave them out and abstention is 18.9%, up just 0.1 points since 2022.

Some places abstain more than their voters' age, education and neighbourhood predict. Lit here: the tenth of polling places with the most of this excess abstention, shown in amber only. Bahia is where a model of who abstains explains least. These are the places to look at more closely: an outdated roll, a hard journey to the polls, or real disengagement.

Everything in this story is a view of the same map. Open Explore to search any municipality, compare years, split abstention by age and filter by neighbourhood or municipality. Share view gives a link to whatever you're looking at.
